meta.description: Curated floor plans of maximum variety for the pilot v2 viewer and for spot checks of the pipeline: drawing styles, eras, building types and the known weak spots (hatching, ornament, columns, open plan, stamps, poché scans). Each plan carries its licence, its permitted use, its scale (where known), its reference (where one exists) and categorical tags from the vocabularies below. Images are copies in data/curated/images (gitignored); this index is tracked. BBL plans go only into data/curated/plans.local.json (same schema, gitignored, never published or sent anywhere). pilot/v2-pipeline/curated.py validates both files and loads the plans; data/curated/README.md explains how to add one.

fields.id: Short stable slug (lowercase, digits, hyphens): source prefix (cc, cvc, wf, cm, syn) and a few words; also the stem of `file`
fields.title: What the sheet shows: building, floor, date of the drawing where known
fields.source: Dataset or archive the image comes from; one value from meta.vocabularies.source
fields.origin: The original file: a path relative to the repository root (a dataset under data/), or the URL it was downloaded from; for renders the IFC model or Swiss Dwellings table the floor was cut from
fields.file: The copy in data/curated/: images/<id>.<ext>, byte-identical to the origin except for renders (synthetic floors, and PDF pages rendered to PNG: origin <pdf>#page=N); a label map that comes with the plan is copied next to it as images/<id>_label.png
fields.licence: Exact licence of this image as stated by its source (per image for Wikimedia Commons, per dataset otherwise; for renders the licence of the model the floor comes from)
fields.attribution: {author, date, page}: author as credited by the source, date of the work as recorded there (null when unknown), and the page to credit; required for `use` attribution and share-alike
fields.use: Whether and how the image may ever be shown publicly; one value from meta.vocabularies.use, implied by the licence (checked by curated.py)
fields.scale: {px_per_m, method}: pixels per metre of the image file and how they are known; px_per_m null and method 'unknown: proposed by the pipeline ...' when the pipeline has to estimate it (the method then names the cues the sheet offers)
fields.reference: {content, source}: what ground truth exists (meta.vocabularies.reference) and where it comes from; curated.load() returns it in image pixels
fields.category: Viewer group (the optgroup in the sheet picker); one value from meta.vocabularies.category, in the order listed there
fields.drawing_type: What kind of drawing the sheet is, by purpose and look; one value from meta.vocabularies.drawing_type
fields.input: How the image was produced; one value from meta.vocabularies.input
fields.wall_style: How walls are drawn (all that apply); values from meta.vocabularies.wall_style
fields.era: When the drawing was made (its graphical conventions), not when the building was built: the date recorded on the source page, otherwise judged from the drawing; one value from meta.vocabularies.era
fields.building_type: Use of the building drawn; one value from meta.vocabularies.building_type
fields.content: What the sheet shows besides walls and openings (all that apply, may be empty); values from meta.vocabularies.content
fields.language: Languages of the text on the sheet as ISO 639-1 codes, or ['none']; values from meta.vocabularies.language
fields.challenges: What the plan tests in the pipeline (all that apply); values from meta.vocabularies.challenges
fields.why: One sentence: why this plan is in the set
fields.render: Only for renders: {floors, floor_id, seed, style}: the floors pickle (path relative to the repository), the floor in it, the random seed and the synth.Renderer style choices that `python curated.py render` uses to draw the image, label map and rooms again
fields.core: true for the core set: the plans the viewer shows and compares across pipeline versions, one per challenge and all publicly showable (use is never "benchmark only"), so that the set stays constant; the other plans serve spot checks (`curated.py run all`) and a local viewer export (`export_viewer.py --local`)

source.CubiCasa5K: Finnish residential plans with SVG ground truth (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.2613548); data/benchmark/cubicasa5k
source.CVC-FP: Residential plan scans with SVG ground truth (de las Heras et al. 2015); data/benchmark/cvc-fp
source.WAFFLE benchmark: Wikimedia Commons plans (SVG, rasterised) with dense masks (Ganon et al. 2025); data/benchmark/waffle
source.Wikimedia Commons: Files from Wikimedia Commons: most from Category:Floor plans of Switzerland (data/benchmark/commons-plans or downloaded for this set), US federal NARA and HABS drawings in data/benchmark/construction-plans
source.US federal drawings: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers standard-design PDFs (vector, public domain under 17 U.S.C. 105), pages rendered at 200 dpi; data/benchmark/construction-plans
source.FloorPlanCAD: Chinese construction CAD drawings, 10 m x 10 m test blocks with line labels (Fan et al. 2021, CC BY-NC 4.0), rendered at 100 px/m with six-class masks; data/benchmark/floorplancad/sample
source.IFC-Bench render: A storey of a permissively licensed IFC-Bench model (data/public/ifc-bench, cut by ifc_prepare.py) drawn whole by synth.Renderer
source.Swiss Dwellings render: A held-out Swiss Dwellings v3.0.0 test floor (data/floors-test.pkl) drawn whole by synth.Renderer
source.BBL: BBL plans: only in plans.local.json, never in the tracked manifest

use.benchmark only: Non-commercial licence (CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-SA): evaluation only; never shown publicly, never used to train or select a deployed model without legal clearance
use.public domain or CC0: May be shown publicly and used freely; credit the source as good practice
use.attribution: May be shown publicly with the credit (author, licence, source page): CC BY, MIT
use.share-alike: May be shown publicly with the credit; adaptations such as overlays under the same licence: CC BY-SA, GPL
use.BBL internal: BBL plans: never published, never sent to external services; plans.local.json only

reference.none: No ground truth: the plan is for visual inspection
reference.walls+openings+rooms: Polygons of walls, doors, windows and rooms (CubiCasa5K and CVC-FP SVG; bench.load_cubicasa, bench.load_cvcfp)
reference.walls+openings+interior: Pixel masks of walls, doors, windows and the building interior (WAFFLE benchmark; bench.load_waffle)
reference.walls+openings+columns+stairs+rooms: The renderer's label map (walls, doors, windows, columns, stairs) and the floor's room polygons, stored with the render
reference.walls+openings+columns+stairs: A six-class label map without rooms: FloorPlanCAD line labels filled (wall, door with its swing, window, stairs; columns from CAD layers, unverified), copied as images/<id>_label.png

category.Construction drawings: Working and construction sheets: dimension chains, axes, door and window tags, section markers, notes, stage overlays
category.FM and safety plans: Area, occupancy, life-safety and security plans: name and area stamps, symbols on a simplified base plan, few dimensions
category.Administrative and public buildings: Parliament, courts, post, council chamber, museum, theatre, observatory: closest to BBL's portfolio
category.Hospitals and hotels: Hospitals, sanatoria, hotels: long corridors of small rooms
category.Industry and transport: Stations, mills, power stations: halls, machinery, columns
category.Monuments and churches: Castles, palaces, churches, convents: massive walls, vaults, ornament
category.Housing: Flats and houses, mostly with ground truth (CubiCasa5K, CVC-FP, WAFFLE)
category.Synthetic renders: Whole floors drawn by synth.Renderer with a complete label map: office, clinic, housing

input.scan grey: Greyscale scan of a drawing or of a printed reproduction
input.scan colour: Colour scan of a drawing (paper tone, coloured inks, pencil, stamps)
input.photo: Camera photograph of a sheet (perspective, uneven light, folds)
input.born-digital raster: Exported from CAD or a drawing program (PNG, JPEG, SVG rasterised): no scan noise
input.vector PDF: PDF with vector content (and possibly a text layer)
input.render: Synthetic render with a known label map

wall_style.poché: Walls filled solid black or dark
wall_style.outlined: Walls as two lines with an empty (or near-empty) core
wall_style.hatched: Walls filled with a hatch or material pattern
wall_style.coloured: Walls filled or drawn in colour
wall_style.single line: Walls as single lines without thickness

era.before 1850: Drawn before 1850: manuscripts, engravings, early lithographs
era.CAD era (1990 onwards): Drawn with CAD or a drawing program
era.synthetic: Render: the style is the renderer's (see render.style)
era.unknown: No date recorded and none judged safely from the drawing

building_type.office/administrative: Offices, parliament, courts, post offices, council chambers
building_type.public/institutional: Museums, theatres, exhibition halls, observatories, libraries, charities
building_type.transport: Railway stations and other transport buildings

content.room stamps: Room names, numbers or letters written inside the rooms
content.area values: Room areas in m² inside the rooms (the stamp-area scale cue)
content.machinery: Machines, turbines, wheels or shafts drawn in plan
content.seating: Rows of seats, pews or benches
content.several drawings: More than one drawing on the sheet (floors, elevation, section, detail)
content.title block: Title, title block or stamp of the office
content.legend: Legend or key to numbers, letters or colours
content.ornament: Ceiling ornament, floor patterns, garden parterres drawn in the plan
content.ceiling lines: Vaults, ribs, beams or skylights projected into the plan
content.colour zones: Rooms or building phases filled with colours
content.site context: Streets, neighbouring buildings, terrain, water around the building
content.annotations: Handwritten notes, pen marks or overlays added to the drawing
content.tags: Door, window, wall-type or room tags: codes in ovals, circles, hexagons or next to openings
content.section markers: Section and detail flags, callout bubbles with sheet references
content.key plan: Key plan or matchlines that tie the sheet to a larger floor
content.notes: General notes, code summaries or construction notes as text blocks or leaders
content.symbols: Fire-safety, security or electrical symbols, usually with a symbol key
content.floor hatches: Floor-finish, tile or paving patterns inside rooms

challenges.baseline: A clean plan in a common style: the control for the others
challenges.hatching that is not wall: Hatched terraces, roofs, floor tiles, paving or terrain next to walls
challenges.ornament: Ornament, vaults or floor patterns inside rooms that can be read as walls or split rooms
challenges.open plan: Rooms separated only by furniture, level changes or virtual lines
challenges.courtyards: Courtyards, light wells or open passages inside the footprint
challenges.thin walls: Partitions drawn as thin or single lines
challenges.massive walls: Very thick masonry or poché masses
challenges.small rooms: Many small cells (offices, hotel rooms, WCs) where one missed wall merges rooms
challenges.several floors: More than one floor on the sheet: the pipeline assumes one floor per sheet
challenges.seating: Seating or pews that can split a hall into small rooms
challenges.overlaid symbols: Electrical layers, machinery or numbers drawn over walls and rooms
challenges.hand lettering: Handwritten or calligraphic labels for OCR
challenges.rotated text: Text upside down or at angles
challenges.site context: Neighbouring buildings, streets or terrain drawn like the building
challenges.non-metric units: Dimensions or scale in feet, Schuh, pieds
challenges.low resolution: Under about 1000 px across: walls only a few pixels thick
challenges.large sheet: Very large or very elongated sheet
challenges.perspective: Photographed sheet: perspective, folds, uneven light
challenges.dimension chains: Dimension chains and extension lines crossing rooms and touching walls
challenges.crossing lines: Axes, section lines, matchlines, routes or overhead edges drawn across rooms
challenges.tags and callouts: Tags, stamps in boxes and callout bubbles: small closed shapes next to or over walls that look like rooms or columns
challenges.complex wall hatches: Material hatches, insulation bands or several hatch patterns in the walls
challenges.inverted polarity: Light lines on a dark ground (blueprints, negatives)
challenges.scale note invalid: The written scale does not hold for the image (reduced or enlarged print)
challenges.renovation overlay: Existing, new and demolished work or construction stages drawn over each other

drawing_type.construction drawing: Working or execution drawing (Werkplan, Ausführungsplan, trade plan): dimension chains, tags, section markers, notes
drawing_type.FM plan: Facility-management style plan: area, occupancy, CAFM, life-safety or security plan on a simplified base plan; stamps with names and areas, symbols, few dimensions
drawing_type.survey drawing: Measured drawing or record plan of an existing building (Bestandesaufnahme, HABS, restoration survey)
drawing_type.permit or design drawing: Design, competition or building-permit plan (Bauprojekt, Baugesuch): rooms, main dimensions, few construction details
drawing_type.publication plan: Plan drawn or reduced for a book, journal, guide or prospectus
drawing_type.marketing plan: Real-estate or sales plan: coloured rooms, furniture, areas, 'not to scale'
drawing_type.diagram: Schematic or reconstruction plan drawn for an encyclopedia or a study (phases, zoning, typology)
